== Biography ==
Andrew Glasgow’s birth is estimated at about 1685; no birth or baptism record has been identified for that estimate.

Andreu Glasgou and [[Cook-36136|Christian Cook]] are indexed as marrying at Kirknewton and East Calder on 14 June 1700.<ref name="AndrewCook1700">"Scotland, Marriages, 1561–1910", FamilySearch ([https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XY9W-VZX XY9W-VZX]), Andreu Glasgou and Christian Cook, 14 June 1700, Kirknewton and East Calder. Transcript inspected 18 October 2026; no image available.</ref>

An index for James Glasgou’s christening at Kirknewton and East Calder on 20 September 1702 names Andreu Glasgou as father. It does not name Andrew’s own parents.<ref name="James1702">"Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564–1950", FamilySearch ([https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQ4K-6MQ VQ4K-6MQ]), Andreu Glasgou in the entry for his son James Glasgou, 1702. Transcript inspected 18 October 2026; image unavailable. The displayed birth-date field contains only "9" and is not a complete birth date.</ref>

== Research Notes ==
=== Kirknewton household review, 20 October 2026 ===

Findmypast transcripts inspected on 20 October 2026 give Andrew Glasgow and Christian/Chtian Cook in banns dated 18 May and 14 June 1700, both OPR 689/20, item 1, p.39. The earlier entry gives both residences only as Kirk Newton and East Calder. Neither names parents or an occupation; no separate solemnization date is supplied. The already cited FamilySearch marriage index gives 14 June. Retain that indexed association with the new banns qualification, without changing a structured date, the record-defined intended-couple grade of 99%, or Andrew’s possible Alexander-3118 father at 58%. The two entries concern one proposed union, not two wives or independent proofs of parentage.

=== Andrew’s Kirknewton father ===

Prefer Alexander [[Glasgow-3118]] as Andrew [[Glasgow-1546]]’s father at 58% subjective confidence, possible. The particular Alexander household is established at Kirknewton by the 1667 Margaret Smith marriage and the father-named Alexander and Agnes entries in 1673 and 1677. Andrew’s 1700 Christian Cook marriage and fatherhood of James in 1702 place his own adult household in the same parish, one generation later. The sustained parish setting and feasible household succession together favour this existing family. Andrew, Alexander and Agnes recur in the descendant branches, providing modest supporting context rather than an independent naming rule. This weighs a specific family against alternatives, rather than inferring fatherhood from surname and estimated ages alone.

The 1685 birth is an unsourced estimate. Taken literally it makes Andrew about fifteen at the indexed 1700 marriage and seventeen at the 1702 christening. Those ages are possible, but they cannot independently support the pedigree. A birth earlier in the 1670s or early 1680s would also fit the adult events and Alexander’s family chronology; no replacement birth year is adopted. Alexander’s own circa-1650 birth is likewise an estimate. The argument rests chiefly on the recorded adult households, not on moving either birth date to fit.

No checked source names Andrew’s father. Another Kirknewton father remains possible: the older Andro account [[Glasgow-1319]], or one of the local John or William households, cannot be excluded merely because no Andrew baptism has been identified. John [[Glasgow-1057]] of Kilwinning/Stevenston remains a weaker comparison because his documented household is elsewhere. Common forenames and the inherited father attachment must not be counted as independent confirmation. The complete sibling and child sequences are not established. Margaret Smith is not assigned as Andrew’s mother.

Check the Kirknewton register around the 1667 marriage and the known 1673/1677 children for an earlier Andrew, and compare residences, witnesses and occupations with the 1700 Cook household. Inspect the original marriage and 1702 child entry when available. These could distinguish Alexander from the surviving local alternatives.<ref name="KirknewtonAndrewReview">[https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XY9W-VZX Andreu Glasgou and Christian Cook, marriage index, 14 June 1700, Kirknewton and East Calder; FamilySearch XY9W-VZX; transcript inspected 18 October 2026, image unavailable]; [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQ4K-6MQ James Glasgou, christening 20 September 1702, Kirknewton and East Calder; named father Andreu Glasgou; FamilySearch VQ4K-6MQ, father entry; transcript inspected 18 October 2026, image unavailable]; [https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XY9W-TPB Alexander Glasgow and Margaret Smith, Kirknewton marriage index, 18 October 1667; previously maintained citation XY9W-TPB, not newly inspected]; [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQ4K-X9V Alexander Glasgow, Kirknewton, birth 7 July and christening 20 July 1673, father Alexander; previously reviewed index VQ4K-X9V]; [https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk/search-records/church-registers Agnes Glasgow, Kirknewton, indexed 28 February 1677, father Alexander; OPR 690,10/77, supplied index row 18; original uninspected].</ref>


=== Kirknewton father review — 31 October 2026 ===

The newly inspected baptism index records John Glasgow, christened 27 May 1709 at Kirknewton and East Calder, with father Andreu Glasgow. That event matches the year, parish and Andrew father already intended by John-81’s inherited identity, while the earlier 39% review had no located record for John himself. Andrew-1546 represents the documented local adult household: Andrew Glasgow married Christian Cook in 1700 and fathered James at Kirknewton in 1702; the held 1714 Andrew child continues that family comparison. The new 1709 John is therefore a specific recorded son fitting that household, rather than only a gap between other children. The adult John/Magdalen Guthrie couple is separately anchored by the 1738 Penicuik marriage and the held West Calder children from 1745 onward, including Andrew in 1747. The marriage was already cited in Magdalene-777’s captured biography; the newly inspected provider transcript confirms that existing adult-family anchor, not a new spouse discovery. Taken together, the recorded father, particular local household and compatible regional adult sequence justify increasing the complete existing father-profile assessment from 39% to 68%, Probable.<ref>Scotland Births and Baptisms, FamilySearch, [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQ4K-6J5 John Glasgow, christened 27 May 1709, Kirknewton and East Calder], father Andreu Glasgow; derivative index inspected 31 October 2026, original image unavailable in inspected view. Birth Date field contains only “5” and is not adopted as a birthday.</ref><ref>Scotland Marriages 1561–1910, Findmypast, [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=SCOT%2FOPR%2FMAR%2F1473346%2F1&tab=this John Glasgow and Magdalen Guthrie], banns 27 May and marriage 23 June 1738, both resident Penicuik, OPR 697/3 item 3 p.52. Provider transcript inspected 31 October 2026, original uninspected. Compare [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XY9J-PJH FamilySearch same-event index] and the marriage already cited in Guthrie-777’s biography; these are not independent witnesses.</ref>

68% includes identification of the indexed Andreu with Andrew-1546 and of the 1709 child with the later John/Magdalen adult. Neither join is directly stated in an inspected original. The inherited 1709 year and parish may derive from this same event and are not counted as independent birth evidence. The baptism index supplies no mother, age, residence below parish level or occupation; its Birth Date field contains only “5”, not a usable birthday. The original image is unavailable in the inspected view. The 1738 provider transcript gives both parties’ residence as Penicuik, banns 27 May and marriage 23 June; it gives no father or age. The shared 27 May day/month is not an identity clue. Other local Johns, another Andrew household, or an unrepresented childhood identity remain alternatives; no missing field excludes them. The marriage index, provider transcript and existing wife biography refer to the same underlying marriage, not independent witnesses. Christian Cook is not upgraded as mother, the circa-1685 Andrew birth and all current vital fields remain unchanged, Andrew’s own father stays 58%, and John’s child Andrew-1333 stays 98%. This strengthens an already attached father, without a new attachment or profile merger.

This proposes a confidence amendment to an existing father, not a new father attachment. No live WikiTree save has been made.
